title: A pixel art pipeline starter for AI agents
author: Trexaty92
selftext:
I have been building a pixel art game, and one problem kept coming up is getting AI to make one good sprite is easy but getting it to make 50 that look like they belong in the same game is a different story.

Proportions shift, characters change between frames, camera angles and lighting drift, colours wander, detail levels don't match. Each sprite might look fine on its own, but put them side by side and they clearly came from different places.

So I've started trying a different approach. Instead of asking an image model to generate every sprite from scratch, the agent builds a simple 3D version of the asset and runs it through the same pipeline every time:

3D model → render → pixel art → sprite sheet

Camera, lighting, palette, and resolution stay locked, so the output stays consistent. And once the 3D asset exists, extra directions and animation frames come out far more predictably.

The part I'm most interested in is the agent side. I don't want to sit in Blender modelling everything by hand. I want to be able to tell something like Claude Code "make a wooden merchant stall with a barrel and some crates" and have it build the asset, run the pipeline, check the result, and keep iterating until it looks right.

One of the main goals is keeping token usage down. Driving Blender through an MCP server works, but the agent burns a lot of tokens on scene state, tool calls, and back-and-forth just to move things around. A small, purpose-built toolset with a fixed pipeline means far less context per asset, which matters once you're generating hundreds of them.

It's not really a 3D modelling tool. It's more a set of tools and a fixed pipeline an agent can operate.

It's still early and rough in places, but I figured some people here might find it interesting:  
[https://github.com/brphillis/threedee-twodee](https://github.com/brphillis/threedee-twodee)

I'm curious how others are dealing with this. Once you're past a handful of assets and into the hundreds or thousands, how are you keeping AI genny art consistent?

comments.author: Bumblemark
comments.body:
Yeah this has been a pain in the ass for me as well. I ended up having it create multiple art guides depending on the type of asset with different pipelines for each so they have their own reference art.   
  
For certain things like walking sprite animation i rely pretty heavily on pixel labs. their mpc has great tools for creating animation sprite sheets, swapping outfits, a whole skeleton-animation tool, etc. So one pipeline is for creating character walking sprites (I have a screen filled with 20-50 little walking sprites with variants of outfits, hairstyles, and colors) where I have a reference base design of that sprite, generate new art with whatever specific outfit on that base model, then run it through the animation tools to generate the sprite sheet.

for buildings in town, i have a seperate guide that gives pixel descriptions of certain geometry that is required, of course a reference art of the town, and again use pixel labs for initial generation and try to make minor corrections without using too much tokens. sometimes i step in and manually adjust the pixel art myself (rarely). But even then this is something i'm still figuring out.

I did try what you recommended before, creating a 3d object via blender and mapping textures onto it but didn't get a good enough outcome consistently for the amount of time/tokens.

Mind you i'm not in the thousands of assets just yet, but i'm getting there and i've wasted way too much tokens on asset generations that'll never see the light of day. But what I've come up with so far is just make sure your pipeline includes specific reference art and hope it does a good enough job

replies.author: Trexaty92
replies.body: Yeah heavy pixel labs user here as well looking for a better solution. Once you have a decent amount of assets a good pipeline like this, or yours can get the job done with claude code or similar. The hardest part is just establishing the 'ruleset with a toolset' which is the specific step im trying to streamline here ( along with avoiding a token churning mcp ) which would be the 'hope is does a good enough job' of your comment.
